before.name: Clayton James
before.description: Clayton James was an artist and World War II opponent of military service who worked in Civilian Public Service camps, including Camp 56 at Waldport, Oregon. In a recorded oral history, he described leaving camp without authorization, arrest by the FBI, jail custody and a trial ending in a suspended sentence. His account identifies his wife Barbara and the archive identifies him as Clayton B. James, CPS worker 004850. His completed jail episode is distinguished from his approximately three years of CPS service. A 2016 obituary identifies the artist as Clayton Bernard James and records his death that year.
